verdict.reason: The code is exactly as the finding describes. cmdReview reads onDiskBefore at spec-to-pr.mjs:949, then unconditionally deletes every round-N directory at :954-958 whenever `--fresh` and not `--dry-run`, and only afterwards computes spentRound/notice and refuses at :974-983. No earlier guard prevents this: reviewArgsError (:605-615) validates only --out/--round/--rebuttals value shapes. Consequently a refused `review --fresh` at the bound has already destroyed all verdict.json carry-forward, and on the next invocation roundsOnDisk (:811-830) returns [], nextRound (:180-186) returns 1, roundBoundNotice(1) returns "" (:228-236), so the bound the code claims only --force can pass (:972-973) is bypassed by simply re-running the command, with priorFindingsFor (:839) now finding nothing. In-lane: a new guard with a reachable bypass plus destruction of state other code paths (priorFindingsFor/pickLatestVerdicts) rely on.

finding.summary: `--fresh` silently bypasses the newly-enforced 3-round bound and discards the carry-forward, so a 4th round can report as a clean round 1
finding.evidence: spec-to-pr.mjs:867 deletes every `round-N` directory and :878 then sets `const onDisk = args.fresh ? [] : roundsOnDisk(base)`, so `nextRound` returns 1 and `roundBoundNotice(1)` is "" — the refusal at :886–887 (`if (notice && !args.force) return fail(notice)`) never fires. `--force` is the advertised, noticed override (self-review.md: "The command **refuses** a fourth round; `--force` exists for the one case that earns it"), but `--fresh` reaches the same place with no warning at all AND additionally throws away every unfixed blocking finding (`priorFindingsFor(base, 1)` is never even called for round 1, spec-to-pr.mjs:900/930). The result a developer sees is `Local review panel: no blocking findings (round 1). The loop can stop here.` on a branch whose round-3 blockers were simply deleted — exactly the false negative the per-lens carry-forward exists to prevent. Either refuse `--fresh` past the bound the way `--force` is required, or at minimum print the bound notice when `--fresh` resets a base that already held `MAX_SELF_REVIEW_ROUNDS` rounds.

verdict.reason: The claimed bypass is not present as described and is explicitly guarded. The finding says the bound is computed from post-deletion state (`const onDisk = args.fresh ? [] : roundsOnDisk(base)`), making `roundBoundNotice(1) === ""`. In fact spec-to-pr.mjs:949 reads `onDiskBefore = roundsOnDisk(base)` BEFORE the `--fresh` deletion at :954-958, and the bound is measured on that pre-delete state at :974 (`const spentRound = args.fresh ? Math.max(round, nextRound(onDiskBefore)) : round`), with the refusal at :975-983 firing on `spentRound` unless `--force`. With 3 settled rounds (MAX_SELF_REVIEW_ROUNDS=3, :152), spentRound=4 and the run is refused with a `--fresh`-specific message naming the rounds it would discard; this also holds under `--dry-run` (nothing deleted, onDiskBefore intact). The scenario is covered by an existing test at spec-to-pr.test.mjs:702-744 asserting `--fresh` alone is refused ("past the self-review bound", "3 rounds have already run") while `--fresh --force` succeeds. The remedy the finding requests is already implemented in its stricter form; `--force` remains the documented, warned override (:984), where discarding carry-forward is the flag's stated purpose. Cited line numbers (867/878/886-887) do not match this code.
